previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, diabetes, and a history of alcohol use presented with acute abdominal pain and dizziness after running out of his home morphine. He was dehydrated and had an elevated anion gap likely due to poor oral intake and mild ketoacidosis. Imaging showed cholelithiasis without acute cholecystitis. He was managed with IV fluids, pain control, and transitioned to oral morphine. His insulin regimen was standardized with Lantus and a sliding scale. He improved clinically, tolerated a diet, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans. Blood and urine cultures showed no infection, and his temperature normalized during the stay.
